The original observation was on wasm32/Pyodide, which is not assumed to be available, so the plan runs on the native host where the transition is expected to be decided by the tmp + 0 idiom on the longdouble path and possibly on float32/float64 depending on compiler behaviour.

oracle.reference_source: regression test test_abs_nan_signbit in numpy/_core/tests/test_umath.py asserting np.signbit(np.abs(dtype(np.nan))) is False
oracle.why: The check is an exact sign-bit comparison on NaN, so no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, np.abs of a positive NaN (for the affected dtype, expected longdouble) returns a NaN with the sign bit set, so np.signbit is True and the assert 'not np.signbit(...)' raises AssertionError; this makes the test fail if the defect manifests on the host.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision using npy_fabs/npy_fabsf/npy_fabsl, np.abs clears the sign bit of NaN for all four dtypes, so np.signbit returns False and both tests pass.
